metadata.title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
top_takeaways: Cardiovascular disease prevention and management in females requires tailored, sex-specific considerations spanning four key life stages: perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4).

Pregnancy is identified as a critical, unique modifying life event that can unmask underlying cardiovascular risk or accelerate cardiovascular disease development (e.g., via adverse pregnancy outcomes).

Optimal female cardiovascular health requires breaking down clinical silos across pediatrics, primary care, OB/GYN, cardiology, endocrinology, and neurology to address interconnected hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health domains.

recommendations.statement: Clinicians providing care to girls and women across clinical specialties should implement female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment strategies organized by the Female Life Stage construct (perimenarche [S1], ovarian cycling [S2], perimenopause [S3], and postmenopause [S4]).

recommendations.statement: Healthcare providers should evaluate pregnancy history and current pregnancy status as a major modifying life event to identify emergent or unmasked cardiovascular risk factors and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
